questions.q: How does a Databricks notebook cell execute, compared to a plain .py script?
options: You run each cell on demand, independently — not automatically top to bottom like a script
It executes automatically the instant the notebook opens
All cells always execute simultaneously in parallel
Cells can only ever be run in the exact order they appear on the page
questions.explain: Each cell's output appears directly beneath it, supporting the run-check-adjust workflow.

questions.q: What does a magic command like %sql at the top of a cell do?
options: Overrides the notebook's default language for that one cell only
Changes the default language for every cell in the entire notebook
Deletes the cell's current output
Has no real effect on how the cell executes
questions.explain: A notebook has one default language, but any individual cell can override it with a magic command.

questions.q: How does registering a DataFrame as a temp view relate to multi-language notebooks?
options: A Python cell's DataFrame, registered as a temp view, becomes immediately queryable from a SQL cell in the same notebook
Temp views only work across separate notebooks, never within the same one
SQL cells cannot access anything created in a Python cell
Temp views are unrelated to notebooks entirely
questions.explain: This makes literal Foundations Lesson 59's point about the DataFrame API and Spark SQL being interchangeable.

questions.q: Why can a notebook that looks correct top-to-bottom on the page still be broken?
options: Cells run in whatever order you actually execute them, not necessarily the order they appear on the page
Notebooks always execute in page order with no exceptions
Because Markdown cells silently corrupt code cells around them
It's impossible for a notebook to be broken if it displays correct-looking code
questions.explain: A notebook run out of order during development can look fine but rely on stale or missing state.

questions.q: What does "Run All" confirm that running cells individually during development doesn't?
options: That the notebook actually works when executed top-to-bottom, in real page order, rather than however it happened to be run before
That every cell's syntax is free of typos
That the notebook is using the Premium pricing tier
That the attached cluster has autoscaling enabled
questions.explain: This directly addresses the cell-order-vs-execution-order trap described in the lesson.
